core.title: Destructive hypermedia requests declare a confirmation
core.given: A markup element that issues a destructive request through the stack's destructive-request construct (newly added or already existing)
core.when: the markup is written, changed or checked
core.then: The element that declares the destructive-request construct MUST also declare, within the stack's gate declaration scope, a confirmation gate (yes/no) or a prompt gate (typed input).
prefer: Declare the confirmation gate on the very element that issues the destructive request, with a message naming what will be destroyed.
For high-value deletions use the prompt gate so the user types something meaningful rather than reflexively confirming (confirmation vs prompt is a product decision about friction).
Express destructive requests with the destructive-request construct so the guard is checkable.
avoid: A destructive-request element with no confirmation or prompt gate declared on it (unguarded).
A confirmation on a neighbouring control, a wrapper or elsewhere in the file — it protects nothing.
A delete expressed as a non-destructive mutation request to a delete-named route, hiding the destructive verb from this rule.
Suppressing, waiving or baselining the finding: this rule is strict (severity 2) — an unguarded destructive request is not suppressible; add the gate instead.
unless: An element carrying the prompt gate instead of the confirmation gate satisfies the rule.
core.why: In hypermedia a destructive request is one declaration on a clickable element: no form submit, route transition or framework guard sits between the click and the request. In a component framework the action passes through a handler, where the confirmation lives and a reviewer sees it; hypermedia removes that handler, so the confirmation must be relocated onto the element as a declarative gate — declarative precisely so it cannot be forgotten — or it is lost in the migration.
evidence: The rule's check reports no element whose gate declaration scope carries the destructive-request construct without a confirmation gate or a prompt gate.
Reviewer confirms the gate is co-located on the same element as the destructive-request construct, not merely present in the file.
No suppression, waiver or baseline entry exists for this rule's findings (disposition strict).
verification: The check finds every occurrence of the destructive-request construct in markup artifacts (new or pre-existing, regardless of the diff), extracts the element's gate declaration scope with a quote-aware scan, and flags the element when that scope carries neither a confirmation gate nor a prompt gate.
The check is CO-LOCATION on the same element, not mere presence of a gate in the file; a gate on a neighbouring control or wrapper does not satisfy it.
Only the destructive-request construct is in scope; non-destructive mutation requests are governed by the companion mutation-progress rule, not this one.
Either a confirmation gate or a prompt gate satisfies the check.

Known blind spot: a destructive action implemented as a non-destructive mutation request to a delete-named route is not detected; that naming choice is invisible to the check, which is why the destructive-request construct should be used.
Disposition strict (generic strict disposition: fails on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline, findings not suppressible); severity 2.

profileRequirements.meaning: The artifact kinds (not file-name suffixes) that count as markup in which declarative request constructs can appear; every destructive-request construct in them is in scope.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's artifact kinds (e.g. static pages, templates, server-rendered output) that count as markup in which declarative request and gate constructs can appear.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: suffix.markup holds only file-name suffixes or name patterns; the Bun scope is given as artifact kinds (template, server-rendered markup), which are not filename selectors, and Bun supplies no suffix list. roles.<role>.kinds is restricted to architectural roles, and markup is not one of the role params.

neutralityNotes: The rule presumes a stack whose markup declares requests and confirmation gates declaratively (hypermedia). All htmx constructs are supplied by idiom.* keys. The markup scope is stated as artifact kinds in bun.json, not as suffixes, so it uses the proposed idiom.markup_kinds key rather than suffix.markup (no Bun suffix values are invented). The detector id, the Bun runtime of the detector, the companion rule id and the concrete markup examples are bunOnly. The 'delete-named route' blind spot is kept generic; the concrete '/…/delete' path is Bun-only.
